review.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
review.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.

e2e.evidence:
WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4) IS REAL EVIDENCE AND IT SETTLES THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR.

THE e2e-desktop JOB CONCLUDED SUCCESS, 3m 35s, on the first Windows execution of a job that had never run. Its annotations, verbatim: "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none (GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-identity rung stays on Ubuntu)" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s".

WHY SUCCESS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FACT RATHER THAN THE COUNTS. The job contains "The desktop axis actually ran" as an ordinary failing step, running assert-desktop-axis-ran.mjs against the run's own JSON report. A Playwright run in which every desktop case skipped exits 0, so a job that merely invoked the suite could have been green while proving nothing -- that guard is what makes success mean the axis executed. It cannot have passed on an all-skipped report, because that is the one case it was built to refuse and was observed refusing locally. So: npm ci succeeded on windows-latest, the browser installed, the two Next servers and the loopback stub ran, openssl resolved without needing the Git fallback this workflow carries, and the desktop-target and cross-target API cases EXECUTED. 118 expected and 0 unexpected matches the Linux development run exactly, which is the right answer for the same suite in the same mode. Retries remain 0; nothing in this change touches playwright.config.ts.

PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause -- "the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu" -- is met, by a run rather than by a parser.

THE PACKAGE JOB CONCLUDED FAILURE, and this round's work is about being able to say why. Its only annotations were "Process completed with exit code 1" and the lifecycle publisher's "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT SENTENCE ASSERTS A CAUSE IT CANNOT KNOW, and that is the defect repaired here. The publisher runs on !cancelled(), so it says that whenever no report file exists -- equally true if the Tauri bundle failed, if the inventory threw "no msi in the inventory", or if the verifier negative check failed. Only two of fourteen steps had an id, so nothing on the run page named the step that exited 1. A reader was invited to conclude the harness refused over a bad --msi. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS, F2 not-run, so the job REGRESSED and the cause is not yet established. Every step now has an id; a "Which step failed" step names the first non-success step with the full trail; and it additionally lists every .msi and .exe actually under the bundle directory, because "tauri-bundle=success" and "there is an installer where the inventory looks for one" are different claims. The old message no longer asserts a cause.

TWO HYPOTHESES WERE ELIMINATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN. (1) PL-0718's tsconfig exclusion of dist was a plausible cause, since the desktop target writes its generated types there: ruled out by deleting .next, dist and next-env.d.ts and running npm run build:desktop on the resulting clean tree, which exits 0 and emits a full route table. (2) The inventory-to-lifecycle path handoff was a plausible cause, since the lifecycle step joins the bundle root with the inventory's name: ruled out by reading artifact-inventory.mjs, which records name as relative(bundleDir, path) -- "msi/<file>.msi" -- so the join is correct, and which already refuses both zero and multiple installers per kind.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED AND IS NOT CLAIMED: the cause of the package failure, and therefore the lifecycle rows for this head. No row is classified as A, B, C or D on this evidence, because classifying from an annotation that admits it does not know would be guessing. The next Windows run of this workflow names the step; that is the evidence, and this gate is not it.

review.title: Corrective: the rate-limit spec assumed a bucket no other worker had touched, and CI is red
review.acceptance:
CI #180 (run 37172243151) IS RED ON A TEST THIS PROJECT SHIPPED IN ROUND 109, and the product is not at fault. The e2e job failed with one error:

  [chromium] > tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts:94:7 > the credential endpoint under repeated attempts > THE FOURTH ATTEMPT IS REFUSED AS THROTTLED, NOT AS A WRONG PASSWORD

REPRODUCED HERE, NOT GUESSED. Running the same two projects with --workers=4 against a real production build and a real PostgreSQL reproduces it exactly, with the spec's own message: 'expected credential rejections followed by a throttled refusal, got [{"status":429,...},{"status":429,...},{"status":429,...},{"status":429,...}]'. All four attempts were throttled.

THE CAUSE. better-auth keys each rate-limit bucket by CLIENT IP AND PATH. Every Playwright worker shares one IP, and `playwright.config.ts` sets fullyParallel with no worker cap, so every spec that signs in -- the watchlist cases, the production-journey cases, `establishSession` itself -- draws from the SAME /sign-in/email bucket this spec is trying to measure. The spec's header already identified that hazard and guarded the EXIT, draining the window in afterAll so it could not poison later specs. It did not guard the ENTRANCE: it assumed it arrived at a bucket nobody had touched, and under parallelism that is simply not true.

THIS IS A DEFECT IN THE MEASUREMENT, NOT IN THE PRODUCT. The limiter did exactly what PL-0719 says it should: four rapid attempts from one address were refused. A spec that reports that as a failure is the fourth instance this project has seen of a new check crying wolf, and the rule is the same -- fix the check, do not relax the control.

REQUIRED: the spec no longer depends on the state of the bucket when it starts. It must OBSERVE its way to a known state rather than assume one.
REQUIRED: both facts are still proven, and still proven to be DIFFERENT facts -- a credential rejection and a throttled refusal. Dropping either, or collapsing them into 'some refusal happened', would discard the entire reason PL-0715 and PL-0719 exist.
REQUIRED: it still proves the 429 carries a usable X-Retry-After.
REQUIRED: it still drains the window before it finishes, so it cannot poison the specs that follow it.
REQUIRED: it is proven under PARALLELISM, not only serially. A green --workers=1 run is what hid this; the evidence must be a run with several workers, in the production configuration, which is what CI does.
REQUIRED: any wait it performs is BOUNDED and fails with a message naming the bucket contention, so a future genuine failure is not mistaken for this one.

MUST NOT: weaken, widen, disable or reconfigure the rate-limit policy. MUST NOT add retries to the Playwright configuration -- `retries: 0` is argued for at length and a retry here would convert a real race into a green mark. MUST NOT serialise the whole suite to make one spec easier. MUST NOT mark the test skipped, or assert something weaker that happens to always hold.
review.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 110 the moment CI #180 was read. PL-0719 is DONE and gpt-architect approved it; this corrective does not reopen that verdict, which was about the POLICY and the product configuration, both of which are untouched and correct. What is wrong is one end-to-end spec delivered alongside it.

P0 because CI is red and a red CI that everybody knows is 'just the flaky auth test' is how a real failure gets ignored.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing. The single allowedPath is e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts, which PL-0719 held and released on completion; no active task names it. Active tasks are PL-0714 (.github/workflows/ci.yml), PW-0208 (apps/desktop/**, docs/LICENSING.md) and PW-0602 (e2e/windows/**, .github/workflows/windows.yml).

typecheck.evidence: npx tsc --noEmit in e2e/: exit 0, no output. The single changed file is e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts, this task's only allowedPath. No product file and no configuration was touched -- in particular playwright.config.ts is unchanged, so retries remain 0 and fullyParallel remains on.

e2e.evidence:
THE FAILURE WAS REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, AND THE FIX WAS VERIFIED UNDER THE SAME CONDITIONS.

BEFORE. npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium --workers=4, production build, real PostgreSQL on 127.0.0.1:5433: 1 failed, 89 passed. The failure is CI #180's, verbatim, with the spec's own message: 'expected credential rejections followed by a throttled refusal, got [{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"}]'. All four attempts throttled, because another worker reached the shared /sign-in/email bucket first.

AFTER, TWICE, same command and configuration: 91 passed, 0 failed (45.1s), and again 91 passed, 0 failed (36.7s). The repaired case takes 8.7s and 9.7s respectively rather than 102ms, which is the waiting-out of contention doing its job and is the visible cost of the repair.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT. The spec no longer assumes it arrives at an untouched bucket; `aCredentialRejection` retries past throttling, BOUNDED at four windows, and returns only once it has actually seen the endpoint examine a credential. The burst then runs from a bucket known to have had room a moment earlier, and a burst of maxRequests+1 in one breath cannot be absorbed by a limit of maxRequests per window however much room there was -- so the throttled refusal is guaranteed whatever other workers are doing. Both facts are still required and still required to be DIFFERENT facts; the X-Retry-After assertion is unchanged; the afterAll drain is unchanged. What was dropped is the assertion that the two refusals appear in a particular order WITHIN ONE ARRAY, because under contention that array's first entry says more about another worker's timing than about this product. The control itself is untouched: no policy value, no configuration, no retry setting, no skip.

THE MECHANISM IN CI IS NOT ONLY PARALLELISM, which is worth recording because it changes what a reader should expect. Playwright defaults to half the cores, so a 2-core GitHub runner runs ONE worker and the suite is sequential there. The bucket is nonetheless contended, because it is a 10-second window and the spec file executed immediately after other files that sign in for real. The repair handles both causes because it observes the state rather than reasoning about who else is running.

ONE THING I FOUND BY OVER-PARALLELISING, REPORTED AS AN ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEFECT. The DEVELOPMENT suite at --workers=4 on this 2-core container fails 6 cases with 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token <, "<!DOCTYPE"' -- the Next dev server returning an error page under on-demand compilation load. At --workers=1, which is what a 2-core CI runner actually uses, the same suite is 118 passed / 24 skipped, which matches CI #180's own development notice exactly. So this is a capacity limit of `next dev` on a small machine, not a product fault, and not caused by this change: auth-rate-limit.spec.ts skips entirely in development.

review.title: A profile remembers which languages its viewer wants
review.acceptance:
PW-0308 REQUIRES PREFERRED AUDIO AND SUBTITLE LANGUAGES 'persisted per profile and consumed as PW-0206's defaults rather than as a second policy', AND THERE IS NOWHERE TO PUT THEM. The profile table carries id, userId, displayName, avatarKey and maxRating; there is no preferences column and no preferences endpoint. gpt-architect's round-110 instruction is explicit: create the smallest backend/data task required, and do not fake persistence with local component state.

THE SHAPE IS ALREADY DECIDED ELSEWHERE AND MUST NOT BE REINVENTED. `subtitlePolicySchema` in packages/contracts/src/domains/subtitles.ts already declares `mode` (auto/off), `preferredLanguages` -- 'Ordered, most-preferred first. Order is meaningful, not a set.' -- and `hearingImpaired`. `PlaybackCapabilities` already declares `preferredAudioLanguages`. This task stores VALUES for those existing fields. A second vocabulary for the same concepts is the 'duplicate language-selection policy' PW-0308 forbids by name.

REQUIRED: a migration that adds the storage. It is additive, it has a default that means 'nothing chosen', and an existing profile keeps working without a backfill -- the 0000 migration's header explains why backfill is the expensive part of a schema decision, and there is nothing here to recover.
REQUIRED: the stored shape is validated on the way IN by a zod contract, like every other contract in this repository, and reuses the subtitle and playback field names and semantics rather than paraphrasing them.
REQUIRED: a language list is ORDERED and the order is preserved through write and read. A store that returns a set has destroyed the only information the field carries.
REQUIRED: read and write endpoints under the profiles API, PROFILE-SCOPED through the same machinery every other profile-scoped route uses. A viewer must not be able to read or write another profile's preferences, and that must be asserted, not assumed.
REQUIRED: 'nothing chosen' is representable and is the default, and is DIFFERENT from 'an empty list chosen'. The player's fallback behaviour depends on telling those apart.
REQUIRED: unknown or unsupported language tags are refused at the boundary with a named reason, not stored and not silently dropped.
REQUIRED: the fail-closed posture of the existing profiles routes is preserved -- a deployment with no identity system refuses rather than serving a default.

MUST NOT: add any field that is not a viewer PREFERENCE. This is not a place to put capability claims, entitlements, rights state or anything a client could assert to widen what it may play. MUST NOT accept a client-supplied profile id in place of the session-scoped one. MUST NOT weaken or bypass the profile scoping in packages/auth's ProfileScope.

OUT OF SCOPE: the settings SCREEN (PW-0308), the player consuming the defaults (PW-0308), and any preference beyond audio and subtitle language behaviour. Parental controls, playback quality caps and autoplay belong to whatever task argues for them.
review.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 110 at gpt-architect's instruction while PW-0308 was being started. The finding that created it: the profile table has no preferences storage, read from packages/persistence/src/schema/profiles.ts rather than assumed.

The more useful finding is what ALREADY EXISTS: subtitlePolicySchema, preferredAudioLanguages and tracks.ts's SubtitlePreferences all carry these concepts today, and apps/web/src/app/watch/watch-session.ts line 205 hardcodes preferredAudioLanguages: ["en"] in CONSERVATIVE_CAPABILITIES. That literal is what a stored preference replaces. Replacing it is PW-0308's, not this task's.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing against PL-0714, PW-0208, PW-0602, PL-0722 and PW-0308. PW-0308 holds the settings tree and the watch route; this task holds persistence, contracts and the preferences endpoint. Disjoint.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck at the repository root: 22 tasks successful, 22 total, exit 0. npm run repo:validate passes. The change spans three packages -- a contract in @liberty/contracts, storage and a repository in @liberty/persistence, and a port, two adapters and an endpoint in apps/web -- and the port is the reason the typecheck is worth more than usual here: LibertyRepository's members are declared as Bound<typeof fn> over the persistence functions, so the three new methods cannot drift from the package signatures, and the in-memory adapter failed to compile until it implemented all three. That is the type system enforcing adapter parity rather than a reviewer noticing.

unit.evidence:
THE SUITES. packages/contracts: 255 tests, exit 0 -- 15 of them new in preferences.test.ts. packages/persistence: 301 tests (1 skipped), exit 0 -- profile-preferences.test.ts adds 12 and the two guard files gained coverage of the new table and the three new repository functions. apps/web: 92 files, 1686 tests, exit 0, up from 90/1659 -- the preferences endpoint's handler.test.ts adds 16 and the db suites now cover three more adapter methods.

THREE GUARDS IN THIS REPOSITORY CAUGHT THREE REAL MISTAKES WHILE THIS WAS BEING BUILT, AND NONE OF THEM WAS WEAKENED.

(1) profile-scoping.test.ts refused the table. The first version declared the primary key with a column-level .primaryKey(), which does not appear in getTableConfig(table).primaryKeys at all -- so the automatic scoping check would have passed the table WITHOUT EXAMINING IT. It is now a table-level primaryKey() with an explicit name, which also satisfies PL-0407's rule that the snapshot, the generated SQL and the database must all say the same word for a constraint.

(2) scope-forgery.test.ts refused forgetMediaPreferences. Written as store.mediaPreferences.delete(profileIdFromScope(input.scope)), the method READS AS issuance-first and is not: JavaScript evaluates the member access before the argument, so against that suite's refusing store it failed with "reached the store" instead of ForgedProfileScopeError -- it had touched storage on behalf of a capability nobody granted. The id is now derived on its own line first. "It refused" and "it refused before touching storage" are different guarantees and the suite exists to tell them apart.

(3) migration-journal.test.ts refused the ninth table, by design. Its EXPECTED_TABLES is a reviewed postcondition that exists because a defect once made db:migrate create ZERO tables while printing success. The set was updated deliberately and the describe block renamed, because leaving it reading "eight-table postcondition" while asserting nine would be a comment that lies.

THE SCOPING ASSERTION WAS ALSO SEEN TO FAIL ON PURPOSE: with the .where() removed from readMediaPreferences, repository-scoping.test.ts fails with "'readMediaPreferences' filters or writes profile_id in every statement" and passes again when restored. That suite renders the captured predicates through Drizzle's own PgDialect, so what it checks is the SQL that would be sent.

THE MIGRATION WAS APPLIED TO A REAL POSTGRESQL, not only generated. A fresh database took 0000 then 0001 cleanly and reports nine tables. \d profile_media_preference shows the columns, the text[] types, PRIMARY KEY btree (profile_id) named profile_media_preference_pkey, and the cascade. A real round trip stored ARRAY['ja','de','en'] and ARRAY['pt-BR','en'] and read back {ja,de,en} and {pt-BR,en} -- ORDER PRESERVED, which is the only information those lists carry. Deleting the profile left 0 preference rows, so the cascade is real rather than declared. The migration itself was GENERATED by drizzle-kit rather than hand-written, with the journal and 0001_snapshot.json it produced, for the reason PL-0407 records: a hand-written snapshot once disagreed with the reviewed migration about three constraint names, which would have emitted DROP CONSTRAINT against a name no database has.

review.title: Corrective: the roving group sets state inside an effect, and repository lint is red
review.acceptance:
`npm run lint` FAILS AT THE REPOSITORY LEVEL on a file PW-0310 shipped in round 109:

  apps/web/src/lib/a11y/roving-group.tsx:198:5
  error  Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders  react-hooks/set-state-in-effect

Confirmed to pre-exist this round's work: stashing the working-tree change and re-running eslint against the COMMITTED file reproduces the same error at the same line. PW-0310's declared gates are typecheck, unit, e2e and architecture-review -- there is no lint gate on it -- so no gate was falsified; the check that would have caught this was not among the ones the task had to run.

THERE ARE TWO setState CALLS IN THAT EFFECT AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS. `setMounted(true)` is a hydration guard: the first client render must reproduce the server's markup, so the arrow-key instruction in `aria-description` may only appear once the keys actually work. `setActive(settled)` writes a CLAMPED index back into state when a shrinking rail has left the stored index past the end.

REQUIRED: the lint error is gone and `npm run lint` is green at the repository level.
REQUIRED: the hydration guard still holds -- the server render must still carry no `aria-description`, and the client must still gain one. Announcing 'use the arrow keys' on a page where nothing is listening for them is a false promise to a screen-reader user, and deleting the guard to satisfy a lint rule would make that promise.
REQUIRED: a stale active index still cannot send focus to a card that is not there. If the write-back is removed, the clamp must move to every point of use -- note that `nextActive` is NOT safe against an out-of-range `current`: ArrowLeft from index 7 in a 3-card rail returns 6.
REQUIRED: the keyboard e2e gate (`e2e/tests/keyboard-reachability.spec.ts`, including its two planted-failure cases) still passes against a real browser. A refactor of focus management that is only unit-tested is not evidenced.

FORBIDDEN: an eslint-disable comment, a rule downgrade or removal in the eslint config, or any change that makes the command green without changing the behaviour the rule is objecting to. The rule is right: a synchronous setState in an effect is an extra render pass on every mount, and the rule cannot tell this one from a cascade.
NOT IN SCOPE: the two pre-existing lint WARNINGS elsewhere in apps/web (`_omitted` and `WatchlistEntryRow` unused). They are warnings, they are not this file, and bundling them here would widen a corrective task into a cleanup.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 110 by claude-lead after `npm run lint` failed during PW-0308's gate sequence. Filed rather than fixed inside PW-0308 because apps/web/src/lib/a11y/** is PW-0310's surface and PW-0310 is DONE: reaching into a closed task's files from an in-progress one would be the silent surface broadening the standing constraints forbid.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck -- 22 tasks successful, 0 failures, at the working tree containing the roving-group change. Also npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json alone: exit 0, no output.

lint.evidence: npm run lint -- exit 0. BEFORE: the same command exited 1 with 'apps/web/src/lib/a11y/roving-group.tsx:198:5 error Calling setState synchronously within an effect can trigger cascading renders react-hooks/set-state-in-effect'. AFTER: '2 problems (0 errors, 2 warnings)' -- the two surviving warnings are the pre-existing unused '_omitted' and 'WatchlistEntryRow', which the acceptance puts out of scope by name. NO SUPPRESSION WAS USED: the repository contains no new eslint-disable comment and apps/web/eslint.config.mjs is unmodified (git status shows it untouched).

unit.evidence: npx vitest run apps/web -- 95 files, 1714 tests, 0 failures. Includes the new apps/web/src/lib/a11y/roving-group.test.tsx (7 tests), which asserts the half neither existing suite could see: the SERVER render carries no aria-description, no arrow-key instruction and no tabindex, for both the ul and div shapes. Its three source rules carry non-vacuity checks -- the effect-body rule asserts the effect was actually found before asserting what is absent from it, so a refactor that renamed the effect fails loudly rather than passing emptily. roving.test.ts (17 tests) and keyboard-reachability.test.ts (25 tests) unchanged and passing.

e2e.evidence: npx playwright test tests/keyboard-reachability.spec.ts --project=chromium --workers=1 against a real next dev server on port 3177 (LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development): 10 passed, 0 failed, 42.4s. The ten include the two PLANTED-FAILURE cases -- 'THE GATE ITSELF FAILS WHEN SOMETHING IS UNREACHABLE' and 'THE ROVING-GROUP CHECK ITSELF FAILS WHEN A RAIL LOSES ITS ENTRY POINT' -- so the suite is proven non-vacuous in the same run, and 'ARROW KEYS MOVE ALONG A RAIL, and Tab then leaves it', which is the behaviour this change refactored. CHROMIUM ONLY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE GATE SURFACE, NOT A NARROWING: ci.yml's e2e job runs 'npx playwright install chromium' and nothing else. The firefox, webkit and mobile-safari projects are UNVERIFIED here -- their browser binaries are absent from this container (browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist at /root/.cache/ms-playwright/firefox-1538/firefox/firefox) and they are not run in CI either. Note on the run: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH had to be pointed at ~/.cache/ms-playwright, because the container's /opt/pw-browsers holds revision 1194 while the pinned @playwright/test 1.62.1 wants 1234; that is an environment fact about this container, not a change to the pinned version.

review.title: Corrective: the lifecycle cross-check demands a literal PW-0307 deliberately removed
review.acceptance:
CI #180's validate job is RED on this, and the product is not at fault. Reproduced locally in full -- `node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs`: 30 tests, 29 pass, 1 fail, 974ms:

  not ok - identity is derived from the files the shell itself compiles > agrees with the install path the Windows workflow asserts
  the Windows workflow does not mention Project Liberty\\liberty-desktop.exe; one of the two has been renamed without the other

NOTHING WAS RENAMED. The case asserts that .github/workflows/windows.yml CONTAINS the literal `<productName>\\<executable>`, on the premise its own comment states: 'That workflow hard-codes Program Files\\Project Liberty'. Commit 9c6abd4 (PW-0307, round 109) deleted that literal on purpose. It replaced an inline `Test-Path` against a written-down executable path with `node scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs`, which DERIVES the paths from apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs. The removed block's own comment gives the reason: the path had already drifted once because it was 'written down in a third place'.

So the workflow moved to derivation -- the better state, and the state this very test's comment says it wants -- and the test still requires the literal the move removed. This is the SIXTH time a check in this repository has reported a fault that was not there, and the standing rule is unchanged: FIX THE CHECK, DO NOT RESTORE WHAT IT MISSES.

FORBIDDEN: putting the executable literal back into windows.yml. That re-creates the third copy PW-0307 removed and re-opens the drift it closed. (It is also not possible from this task, which does not own that file -- stated so the reasoning is on the record rather than the surface restriction being the only reason.)
FORBIDDEN: deleting the case. A cross-check between the derived identity and the workflow is worth having; what is wrong is WHICH fact it cross-checks.

REQUIRED: the case asserts a correspondence that is actually true of the current arrangement, and would still catch a rename. windows.yml line 333 still carries `Join-Path ${env:ProgramFiles} "Project Liberty"` -- the productName literal survives, the executable literal does not -- so the install ROOT is still cross-checkable against IDENTITY.productName.
REQUIRED: the case's comment is corrected rather than left describing the arrangement it was written against. A comment that outlives the code it describes is how this repository keeps losing things, and the wrong premise is recorded at the line that held it.
REQUIRED: non-vacuity. The new assertion must be shown to FAIL when the workflow and the derived identity disagree, not merely to pass today -- an `includes` against a string that is absent from both would pass forever.
REQUIRED: the executable's disappearance from the workflow is NOT quietly accepted as untested. Either name where that correspondence is now proven -- verify-install.mjs derives it from sidecar.rs and windows.yml invokes that -- or state plainly that it is proven on a runner and not here.
review.notes: FILED ROUND 110 by claude-lead after reading CI #180's validate JOB page, which reports FAILED while the run page reports passed. Found only because gpt-architect's round-110 instruction said to read the job page. scripts/windows/** is reserved by PW-0501 and PW-0107 (both DONE) and PW-0502 and PW-0503 (both READY and unowned), so nothing active collides.

unit.evidence:
node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 32 tests, 7 suites, 32 pass, 0 fail, 206ms. BEFORE: 30 tests, 29 pass, 1 fail -- "agrees with the install path the Windows workflow asserts", the case CI #180's validate job went red on.

NON-VACUITY PROVEN THREE WAYS, because the case this replaces passed for a whole round while asserting something that was no longer true, and "it is green now" is exactly what it said then.

1. AGAINST THE REAL FILE, EXECUTABLE. sed -i 's/liberty-desktop.exe/liberty-player.exe/' scripts/windows/verify-install.mjs, then re-run: 32 tests, 31 pass, 1 fail -- "not ok 6 - verify-install's executable agrees with the derived executable". File restored from a copy taken first; git diff --stat on it is empty afterwards.

2. AGAINST THE REAL FILE, PRODUCT NAME. sed -i 's/"Project Liberty"/"Liberty Player"/' .github/workflows/windows.yml, then re-run: 32 tests, 31 pass, 1 fail -- "not ok 5 - the workflow's install root agrees with the derived product name". Restored the same way; git diff --stat empty.

3. IN THE SUITE ITSELF. A third case, "A CROSS-CHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL IS NOT A CROSS-CHECK", drives the same comparison function with disagreeing text and requires the refusal, and then with agreeing text and requires that it does NOT throw -- so the rule is not satisfied by a function that always throws. That one runs on every future execution; 1 and 2 were performed once, by hand, and are recorded here rather than left as a claim.

WHAT THE FIX DID NOT DO. No literal was restored to .github/workflows/windows.yml -- git diff --stat shows it unmodified -- so PW-0307's third copy stays removed. The case was not deleted: it now guards the two correspondences that actually exist, the product name in the workflow and the executable in verify-install.mjs, which is the copy PW-0307 could not eliminate because the name comes from Cargo.toml's binary name rather than from a Rust constant. The old case's false premise is recorded at the lines that held it rather than quietly dropped.

recommended.title: Trusted-proxy topology and how this deployment derives a client IP
recommended.acceptance:
THE HAZARD, AND THE RULING THAT CREATED THIS TASK. PL-0719 found that better-auth keys each rate-limit bucket by client IP and path, and that when it cannot resolve a client IP it falls back to a SINGLE LITERAL KEY for every caller -- three sign-ins per ten seconds for the entire deployment. Behind a reverse proxy with no trusted-header configuration, that is the live behaviour.

PL-0719 reported it rather than fixing it, and gpt-architect's round-110 security review confirmed that was correct and ruled: DO NOT trust X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded, X-Real-IP or similar headers by default; a shared fallback bucket when the client IP cannot be trusted is SAFER than accepting a spoofable header that gives an attacker per-request rate-limit evasion.

SO THIS TASK IS NOT 'TURN ON FORWARDED HEADERS'. It is: decide, write down and enforce WHICH HOP MAY ASSERT A CLIENT ADDRESS, so that forwarded-client-IP semantics are enabled only where a deployment has explicitly defined that.

REQUIRED: the trusted-proxy topology is STATED IN THIS REPOSITORY -- which proxy hops are trusted, how they are identified, and what the default is when nothing is configured. The default must remain not-trusting, because that is the direction in which being wrong is survivable.
REQUIRED: an untrusted forwarded header is IGNORED, not merged, not partially honoured and not logged as if it were the client. A header from an untrusted hop is an attacker-supplied string.
REQUIRED: the direct-client case -- no proxy at all -- derives the address from the connection and is tested.
REQUIRED: the proxied case, with a configured trusted hop, derives the client address correctly and is tested, including a chain longer than one hop.
REQUIRED: A SPOOF TEST. A caller that supplies its own X-Forwarded-For must NOT be able to change which bucket it lands in. This is the test the whole task exists for and it must be seen to fail against a naive implementation.
REQUIRED: A RATE-LIMIT IDENTITY TEST. Two callers the policy should treat as distinct get distinct buckets, and one caller cannot become many by varying a header.
REQUIRED: the shared-bucket fallback remains reachable and is still correct when no trusted topology is configured. Removing it in favour of trusting something is the failure this task exists to prevent.

MUST NOT: trust any forwarded header by default, under any configuration shortcut, environment-variable convenience or development-only carve-out. MUST NOT weaken, widen or disable the rate-limit policy PL-0719 established; this task changes WHO a request is attributed to, never how many requests are allowed. MUST NOT introduce a header or parameter that lets a caller nominate its own identity for any purpose.

OUT OF SCOPE: geo-IP, IP reputation, blocklists, and any other use of a client address beyond rate-limit identity. Deriving the address correctly is this task; what else might be done with it is not.
recommended.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 110 at gpt-architect's explicit instruction in the PL-0719 security verdict: "Create a separate deployment-security task if one does not already exist: define trusted-proxy topology and client-IP derivation. Only enable forwarded-client-IP semantics when the deployment explicitly defines which proxy hop is trusted." The verdict states the follow-up does NOT block PL-0719, which is DONE.

Board searched before filing: no task names a proxy, a forwarded header or client-IP derivation in acceptance or notes. PL-0719 (DONE) owns the rate-limit POLICY and names this hazard; it is listed here as a review dependency rather than an allowed path, so this task can be read against it without reserving it.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing. Active tasks are PL-0714 (.github/workflows/ci.yml), PW-0208 (apps/desktop/**, docs/LICENSING.md), PW-0602 (e2e/windows/**, .github/workflows/windows.yml) and PL-0720 (one e2e spec). None names anything under packages/auth or docs/DEPLOYMENT_TRUST.md. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts and index.ts were PL-0719's and PL-0719 is now DONE.

P1 and not P0: the current behaviour FAILS CLOSED -- a shared bucket is restrictive, not permissive -- so nothing is open today. What is missing is the topology decision, and the danger is that somebody closes the availability gap by trusting a spoofable header, which would be strictly worse than the gap.
